questions.q: What kind of object is `current` inside a Business Rule script?
options: A real GlideRecord pointed at the exact record being processed
A plain JavaScript string containing the record's sys_id
A read-only JSON snapshot that cannot be modified
A client-side DOM reference to the form
questions.explain: current is a genuine GlideRecord, so ordinary dot-notation field access and GlideRecord methods both work on it directly.

questions.q: In this Before rule, what happens to the change made to current.resolved_at?
options: It's folded into the save automatically, with no need to call current.update()
It has no effect because Before rules cannot modify fields
It requires calling current.insert() explicitly to take effect
It only applies the next time the record is saved
questions.explain: Because this runs before the write, any field changes made to current become part of the same save automatically.

questions.q: Under what conditions is `previous` populated and meaningful inside a Business Rule?
options: Only on update operations, and only when the rule's Advanced checkbox is enabled
On every operation type, always, with no configuration needed
Only on insert operations, since that's the only 'before' state that exists
Only when the Business Rule's timing is set to Display
questions.explain: previous represents the pre-update snapshot, which only exists for updates, and ServiceNow only populates it when Advanced mode is turned on.

questions.q: What does this condition correctly detect?
options: That the incident's priority specifically just escalated to 1, not merely that it was already Priority 1 before this save
That the incident was just created for the first time
That the incident's priority has never changed in its history
That the current save is an async operation
questions.explain: Checking previous.priority != 1 alongside current.priority == 1 is what distinguishes an actual escalation from a save of a record that was already at Priority 1.

questions.q: Why would checking only `current.priority == 1`, without comparing to `previous`, be a mistake in an after-update escalation rule?
options: It would fire on every single save of an incident that's already Priority 1, not just the moment it escalated
current.priority is never actually populated on update operations
It would cause the Business Rule to fail to save entirely
It would make the rule run only on insert instead of update
questions.explain: current alone only shows the new value — without previous, there's no way to tell a fresh escalation apart from an unrelated save of an already-escalated record.
